items.prompt: What does this capstone's empirical 85% loss VaR mean?

options.why: A quantile does not bound every future outcome.

options.text: A specified lower empirical loss quantile
options.why: The rank/method, sample, unit and horizon are part of its meaning.

options.text: An amount exceeded by exactly 15% of the observed losses in every dataset
options.why: A lower empirical quantile can have a boundary atom, so the strict exceedance fraction need not equal 15%.

options.text: The average of losses strictly above the empirical quantile
options.why: That is a tail average with its own boundary convention, not the quantile itself.

items.explanation: The empirical quantile is defined by a finite sample convention and does not prove future population coverage.
